walkthroughs.body_html:
Market research stops you wasting money on a product no one wants.

It tells you:

  • What customers like.
  • What price feels fair.
  • What rivals are doing.

Skip research and you might end up with a warehouse of unsold trainers. 👟

Primary research is new — you do it yourself:

  • Surveys.
  • Interviews.
  • Focus groups.

Secondary research is data already out there: government stats, magazine articles, rival websites.

Once the product is selling, feedback rolls in: reviews, ratings, returns.

Smart businesses read every review. They fix what's broken and praise what works.

Apple, McDonald's and Nike all change products based on customer feedback. 🌟

What is corporate governance, and how does it differ from CSR?
options: Corporate governance is the same as corporate social responsibility.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Corporate governance is the legal requirement to have a CEO.

Corporate governance is the system of rules, practices and processes by which a company is directed and controlled — focusing on accountability, board structure and shareholder rights. CSR is about wider social/environmental responsibility.
